findings.title: 'Bounded' thermal record is bounded per container, not per record
findings.detail: _jsonable caps each ndarray/list/tuple at MAX_RECORD_ARRAY elements but applies no cap to Mappings, and nesting multiplies the limit. A whitelisted field (tj_max_node, nodes, picard, energy_balance) can therefore carry a list of several 9,999-element arrays, or a dict with any number of keys. The docstring's 'so nodal fields cannot reach the checkpoint' holds only for a single flat container. The six-field whitelist and the rejection of any single mesh-sized array keep the practical exposure small.
findings.evidence: _thermal_record accepted tj_max_node=[np.zeros(9999)]*3 with picard={'history':[np.zeros(9000)]*50} (2,400,271 JSON bytes), and picard={str(i):0.0 for i in range(200000)} (2,889,059 bytes).
findings.suggested_check: Count total leaf elements across the whole record, including dict entries, and cap that total.

findings.title: Multibyte torn-line test cannot tell byte offsets from character offsets
findings.detail: Store.get writes json.dumps output with ensure_ascii, so everything before the last newline is ASCII and the character index of the cut equals the byte index. test_torn_multibyte_line_truncates_at_the_byte_offset would also pass with a character-offset os.truncate. Separately, test_torn_line_repair_never_rewrites_the_file blocks write_text/write_bytes but not path.open('w'), although its comment says it does. The implementation itself is correct because it works in bytes.
findings.evidence: Reproducing the test's file gave b'{"k": "\\u00e9", "v": "\\u00fc"}\n{"k": "\xc3\xb6", "v": ' with byte cut 31 and character cut 31.
findings.suggested_check: Put a raw non-ASCII complete line before the torn tail so the two offsets differ.

findings.title: Store load crashes when a torn tail is split inside a UTF-8 character
findings.detail: json.loads(raw[cut:]) raises UnicodeDecodeError, a ValueError but not a JSONDecodeError, so the repair branch is skipped and Store.__init__ crashes. The driver's own writer emits only ASCII, so only outside corruption (e.g. garbage bytes after a crash) can reach this. Behaviour is unchanged from before (read_text also raised).
findings.evidence: Appending bytes '{"k": "' + 0xC3 to a valid checkpoint made Store(p) raise UnicodeDecodeError, and the file was left untouched.
findings.suggested_check: Catch ValueError (which covers UnicodeDecodeError) in the repair branch.

findings.title: band_e_R duplicates mfos.metrics.ratio_band_estimate
findings.detail: The driver has one estimator, but it is a copy of the evaluator's function rather than an import of it, even though the driver already imports gci_capped from mfos.metrics. They are identical today; the copies could drift.
findings.evidence: On 100,000 random five-level pairs, including monotone, oscillating and diverging thickness sequences, max |band_e_R - ratio_band_estimate| = 0.0.
findings.suggested_check: Import ratio_band_estimate in search.py, or add a test that pins the two to each other.

findings.title: Near-tie band solves cover only the twin-based window (outside this change)
findings.detail: The evaluator's reconstruction-based secondary column switches the K1 near-tie band to w_ind = 2 e_R(ind, reconstruction) + s_ref (row contract item 9). The driver band-solves near ties only within the twin-based window. If e_R(ind, recon) > e_R(ind, twin), five() would find missing band columns and raise. This predates the change.
findings.evidence: tools/mfos/mfos/metrics.py lines 617-622 compared with search.py lines 397-403; research/o003/e008_row_contract.md item 9.
findings.suggested_check: Band-solve the union of the twin-based and reconstruction-based near-tie windows, or record that the secondary K1 column may be unavailable.

independent_checks_performed: Ran every required check: tests/unit/optimize 36 passed; fast unit tests 776 passed (39 deselected); ruff clean; thermal_fem.py sha256 prefix a216d5fe3209bcee matches; mfos gate --fast: all gates passed.
Searched with git grep for callers of Solvers/run_search/run_control: none outside the optimize tests, so removing the injected e_R breaks no caller.
Compared band_e_R with mfos.metrics.ratio_band_estimate on 100,000 random five-level pairs, including monotone, oscillating and diverging thickness sequences: max abs difference 0.0.

Checked the driver against the evaluator's headroom code (metrics.py lines 601-623) and the O003 K1/A1 text: w_ind, the levelling test and the near-tie window use the same formula (2 e_R(ind, twin) + s_ref with P3's estimator on the ratio).

Torn-checkpoint simulation over a full run_search (233 records): cut the file mid-record after 3, 116 and 232 records and resumed. New solves were exactly 230, 117 and 1; rows, w_ind, near_ties and a1_best matched a fresh run; the file ended newline-terminated.
Size-limit probes: nested arrays (2.4 MB) and a 200k-key dict (2.9 MB) were accepted by _thermal_record.
Torn-tail probe: a tail split inside a UTF-8 character makes Store raise UnicodeDecodeError.

Test-the-tests: showed the multibyte torn-line test has byte cut = character cut = 31, so it cannot catch a character-offset bug; checked mutations (comparing against the reference instead of the twin, near ties against the wrong comparator) and found the e_R tests would catch them.

Read thermal_fem.ThermalResult: it has no tj/tj_max_node/fingerprint/picard fields, so a raw result fails loudly (ValueError) and an adapter is required; its field nodes holds coordinates, not counts.
caveats: 'Bounded thermal records' means a whitelist of six fields with a 10,000-element cap per individual array or list. It is not a cap on total record size: dicts are uncapped and nesting multiplies the limit.

The atomicity of the repair is checked against a process being killed (a single os.truncate call, or a one-byte append). There is no fsync, so durability after a power loss is not covered, and two processes appending to the same checkpoint at once are not protected.
Thermal records loaded from checkpoints written before this change are reused without the whitelist or required-field check.

The driver does not check that the record's fingerprint matches the layout's, does not check the shape of tj_max_node or nodes, and silently drops dies from a ragged tj (behaviour that predates this change). The evaluator's gated sanity checks must catch these.
A thermal adapter must supply node counts under the name nodes; ThermalResult.nodes holds node coordinates.
